headline: High-risk default interaction: Dify can execute and exfiltrate content, while awesome-prompts is an unverified prompt source that may be ingested as instructions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a content-writing prompt repository, and Dify wires tools into agent/workflow apps with file inputs and shared datastore. If prompts or files from agent_a are fed into agent_b as instructions, injection is plausible in default orchestration. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF agent_a content is copied into agent_b prompts or knowledge-base files
IF agent_b treats uploaded file text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Separate prompt libraries from executable agent prompts
Prefix imported content as untrusted data
Add a review step before any prompt is activated
Restrict agent_b to read-only ingestion for prompt repositories

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b has broad network egress, reads/writes filesystem, and handles conversation logs and knowledge-base files; agent_a is docs-only and touches no data classes. If agent_a content is uploaded into agent_b, that content can flow to model providers or tool APIs. The pair lacks a documented isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts are uploaded into agent_b knowledge-base files
IF agent_b forwards those files or logs to external model providers or OpenAPI tools
mitigations: Do not upload sensitive prompt corpora into agent_b
Disable external tools for imported content
Use a separate workspace for prompt repositories
Review retention settings for conversation logs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or execution surface, while agent_b can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource between them in the profiles, so direct conflict is limited. The only plausible conflict is indirect through shared operator-managed files, which is unusual and small in blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF operator scripts let agent_a-generated text be written back into agent_b-managed files
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Make agent_a outputs read-only artifacts
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
Disable write access for agent_b when processing prompt catalogs

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces prompt content that agent_b can ingest through workflow wiring, and agent_b can then act on that input via tools or model-provider calls. If agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative, errors or malicious instructions can cascade into downstream actions. Because Dify supports tool use and agent workflows by default, the pathway exists without special setup.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as a system or developer prompt
IF agent_b executes tools or sends API calls based on that output without verification
mitigations: Insert a verification step before tool execution
Require human approval for high-impact actions
Mark agent_a output as untrusted input
Log and diff any prompt transformations before execution

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for agent_a, while agent_b stores conversation logs and knowledge-base content. The only concrete compliance concern is that imported content may be retained in agent_b logs or datastore, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated data class. This is a limited, documentation-only gap.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_b conversation logs or knowledge-base files
IF retention settings are left at their documented defaults
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in agent_b logs
Set explicit retention limits
Purge imported knowledge-base files after use
Document data-class handling for each workflow
